allImages.caption: Today Quakers are well-known for their staunch support of the Abolitionist movement during the 1800s. However it took at least a century to get Friends to agree as a whole to take up this cause. In April 1688, four German and Dutch Quakers, Francis Daniel Pastorius, Garret Henderich, and brothers Derick and Abraham op de Graef (cousins to William Penn) created a petition against slavery and presented it to their local meeting in Germantown, Pennsylvania.
